newsitem.title: GREECE: Long-run ecu/drachma vols steady as spot ranges.
newsitem.headline: Long-run ecu/drachma vols steady as spot ranges.

text.p: Implied volatilites for long-dated ecu/drachma options were flat as the ecu/drachma cross was hovering in the 310.40/80 channel and softer drachma rates discouraged investors from opening new positions depressing volume, dealers said.

"Implied volatilities for long-run ecu/drachma options hold unaffected by a rangebound spot," said a senior options trader at private Alpha Credit Bank. "Volume is subdued as lower drachma rates discourage investors from opening new positions."

Tighter interest rate differentials between the drachma and other EMS currencies coupled with more volatile spot EMS/drachma crosses have made the risk-reward profile of EMS/drachma options less attractive, he said.
"Investors show no interest in opening positions in short-dated ecu/drachma options," said the dealer. "Also, there seems to be little interest in low-delta ecu/drachma options."
Ecu/drachma and mark/drachma options are the most popular forex options with local investors.
Implied volatilities for one-month ecu/drachma and mark/drachma options were steady at 3.0/5.0 percent and 4.0/6.5 percent respectively, the dealer said.
Implied volatilities for one-year ecu/drachma and mark/drachma were also unchanged at 7.5/9.5 percent and 8.5/11 percent, he said.

"Risk reversals were skewed towards ecu/drachma puts in the first four months of 1997 when trading volume was bigger but tend to balance out lately," the dealer said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
